short_summary: Bournemouth is unhappy after midfielder Alex Scott picked up a thigh injury while playing for England. However, England coach Thomas Tuchel insisted that the medical staff took zero risk.

sources.name: BBC Sport
sources.title: Bournemouth unhappy after Scott injured with England

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.title: Bournemouth unhappy over Scott injury but Tuchel says England took ‘zero risk’

paragraphs: Football clubs and national teams often face disagreements over player fitness during international breaks. Recently, Bournemouth expressed frustration with the England national team regarding the handling of midfielder Alex Scott. According to reports, the twenty-three-year-old player could now be absent for up to eight weeks due to a quadriceps issue.

Scott felt some discomfort in his thigh before a match against Croatia. Despite this issue, he played seventy minutes in central midfield before being substituted. England coach Thomas Tuchel described the situation as a strange one during a news conference. Tuchel stated that the player trained fully and gave green lights, adding that the medical department took zero risk. According to Tuchel, when the player was asked if he wanted to come off during the game, he said no and felt that he could have finished the ninety minutes.

However, sources indicated that there is significant disappointment at Bournemouth because the national team staff knew about the thigh problem. As a result of this injury, Scott will likely miss numerous upcoming matches for his club in both the Premier League and European competitions.

In addition to Scott, Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa also left the England squad as a precautionary measure. Tuchel explained that Konsa had experienced discomfort that eventually caused light trauma, meaning the player needed to return to his club for proper medical treatment. Both situations highlight the physical challenges and pressures that professional football players face during a busy sports calendar.

facts.fact: Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott suffered a thigh injury while playing for the England national team.
Scott could be out for six to eight weeks due to the quadriceps issue.
England coach Thomas Tuchel stated that the national team took zero risk with the player's health.
Bournemouth is unhappy with how England handled the midfielder's pre-existing thigh discomfort.
Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa also left the England camp due to a quad injury.
